Further_comments: South of Svartenuten in Buerdalen is a wide-dammed lake at an altitude of 1200 m. On October 9, 2002, it was observed that the wide-dammed water had been emptied. Small lake (1200 m.) 2 km S of Buerbreen, draining to Buervatn and Sandvenvatnet in Odda.. Observed by HAE October 10, 2002. Event probably took place during the summer, most likely August. Measured height of shoreline, water level dd, and elevation profile on the glacier. Estimated water volume approx. 1 million m3., height 30-40 meters, distance to outlet approx. 500 meters, outlet approximately the same height as the bottom of the lake. Wind trough along the mountain, possible drainage there in the early phase. Signs of a glacier at the opposite end of the lake, and cracks on the glacier surface. No signs of flooding further down the watercourse (but fresh snow on the ground). Based on observations made on 20 September 2003, it did not appear that the water level in the lake had changed since October 2002. A new inspection on 9 August 2004 showed that the glacial lake was empty of water, probably unchanged since September 2003. Photos were taken for documentation. Floods can primarily affect settlements in Buerdalen, Odda municipality. People from there contacted NVE in 1996/97 with questions about whether there could have been an incident there previously. An inspection in August 1997 (HAE) showed that the lake was full, no traces of a jökulhlaup (HAE).

Further_comments: A glacier flow that appeared to come from Stigaholtbreen was discovered when Even Loe, hydrologist at Statkraft AS in Gaupne, saw that the river in Jostedalen was very brown in the last week of August. When he investigated further, he saw that it was the river from Stigaholtbreen that was "brown, flood-sized and thick as porridge" while all the tributaries to Jostedøla were blue-green with little water flow. Water flow from Stigaholten was not estimated, but there was much more water in Stegaholtbreelvi than from Lodalsbreelvi, the river in Stordalen southwest of Stigaholtbreen. An inspection showed clear traces of water and gravel/sand on Stigaholtbreen from a bottom glacier west of the tongue of Stegaholt, and that the snow on the glacier had been washed away. There was no sign on the surface of the bottom glacier that there had been water there, so the water must have been under the ice. Aerial photos from 2010 show signs that it has happened several times before
